newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary PM says devaluation peg could change in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hungary PM says devaluation peg could change in 1997.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Friday that if the economy continues to improve the monthly 1.2 percent crawling peg devaluation could be revised downward in early 1997.
"There is a question which has been raised several times regarding the crawling peg devaluation policy and whether we should change it or not," Horn said during an economic forum in Budapest.
"I think this should be dependent on the results we will achieve in the first months of 1997."
Horn said his socialist-led government had made great strides in bringing down inflation which had reached a peak of 30 percent a year to between 23 and 25 percent this year.

"We have to combat inflation because it is a well-known fact that we had an average 25 percent inflation and there is no other choice for us, we have to carefully take into account the offer and the demand," Horn said.
The crawling peg devaluation was introduced as part of the government's austerity package in March 1995 as a means of devaluing the then-overvalued forint in a controlled and predictable way.
The devaluation was initially fixed at 1.3 percent per month but was reduced to 1.2 percent per month in January.
